newsitem.title: USA: Salvi's parents want probe of his death.
newsitem.headline: Salvi's parents want probe of his death.

text.p: The parents of abortion foe John Salvi, convicted of murdering two health clinic workers, asked state and federal officials Monday to investigate his death at a Massachusetts maximum security prison.

"Prison officials are supposed to be watching out for people. They're supposed to be responsible. We called to see if he was all right and they would say it's none of their business," Salvi's father, also named John, told reporters.
He called conditions at the Walpole, Mass. prison "inhuman ... You hear about this in Russia and other countries but that's here in Massachusetts."
His wife Anne-Marie wept as lawyer James Sultan described her son's "swollen face" during an October visit. Sultan said Salvi told him other prisoners had beat him.

Mrs. Salvi said she repeatedly called the prison to find out if her son had received the long underwear, regular underwear and two pairs of socks she had sent. She said prison officials told her "that's confidential information."
Salvi's chief defence lawyer J.W. Carney meanwhile questioned for the first time whether his client's death was really a suicide.

"His feet were tied. His hands were tied together. There was cotton stuffed in his mouth and a plastic bag over his head," Carney said of Salvi, who was found dead in his cell Friday. "The suicide of John Salvi requires more than a comment from a corrections spokesman that his death is not inconsistent with suicide," Carney said.

Carney said he asked that Gov. William Weld appoint a special commission to investigate mental health evaluations of state inmates and also sought to have Salvi's death probed by the U.S. attorney for Massachusetts.
"We understand a request for an investigation has been made," said Joy Fallon, a spokeswoman for U.S. Attorney Donald Stern. "We will review it."
A Weld spokesman referred all questions to the state's corrections department. Officials there did not return calls seeking comment.

Salvi, 24, shot seven health care workers -- including the two who died -- in the Boston suburb of Brookline. He was serving a sentence of more than two life terms for the worst violence at abortion clinics in the nation.
